strand_a.title: The quest for European autonomy and the risks of EU and NATO precarity
strand_a.summary: While Europe has long debated the need for greater strategic autonomy, recent crises and the U.S.’s partial disengagement from European security have intensified expectations for Europeans to assume more responsibility on security and defense. However, the collective European rights and resources within these existing organizations have not kept pace creating a paradox: as the EU and NATO have expanded their roles on matters related to European security, they have experienced increased precarity, failing to deliver on transformative resilience toward a more autonomous Europe. As the EU and NATO confront their ontological insecurities, precarity has deepened, undermining transformative resilience.

strand_a.title: Balancing blue growth and the ecosystem approach: policy coherence in Sweden’s Marine Spatial Plan for the Baltic Sea
strand_a.authors: Oliver Kaspersson, Karina Barquet, Sandstrom Camilla
strand_a.summary: Fisheries emphasise socio-economic resilience but are weakly integrated with spatial planning and conservation measures. There is growing expectation within the European Union (EU) that Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) – the public process for allocating marine space among competing uses – can support environmental restoration and economic development through the Ecosystem Approach (EA), which seek to balance ecological, social, and economic objectives. Building on Malawi Principle 3 of the Convention on Biological Diversity, the analysis assesses policy coherence across governance levels (global and EU policies to national planning) and across key sectors (offshore wind, fisheries, and shipping).

strand_a.summary: The study examines how strategic considerations influence green relocation decisions for value chain steps in energy-intensive industries located in renewable energy resource-scarce regions. strand_a.authors: Maria Bolboaca, Guido Cozzi, Silvia Galli
strand_a.source: Journal of International Money and Finance
strand_a.summary: This paper examines how international tax harmonization affects the trade-off between domestic innovation and foreign direct investment (FDI) in small open economies. Focusing on Hungary and Ireland—two countries with low corporate tax rates and high FDI exposure—we simulate reforms inspired by the European Union’s global minimum tax initiative. strand_a.summary: This paper argues that effective risk assessment requires moving beyond a static view of government as a rule‐maker to analyzing it as a dynamic, strategic actor. We develop a tripartite framework that enables managers to evaluate regulatory risk by analyzing a state's discursive commitments (public narratives and policy signals), institutional capacity (administrative design and enforcement power), and material leverage (control over key technological infrastructure). Applied to the landmark European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, the framework reveals critical “orchestration gaps” between a state's regulatory ambitions and its infrastructural dependencies.

strand_a.title: New Delhi's BRICS: An Economic Agenda Europe Can Use | ISPI
strand_a.summary: Commentary Asia · Geoeconomics by Soumya Bhowmick whatsapp The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration , adopted unanimously at the close of the 18th BRICS Summit on 12–13 September, is most usefully read for the agenda it chose to prioritise. The common thread is credit enhancement and de-risking to mobilise private capital rather than balance-sheet expansion, which is the same instrument logic that underpins Global Gateway and Italy’s Mattei Plan. Critical minerals are framed around value addition and sovereign control of resources, energy security around uninterrupted flows and the protection of cross-border infrastructure, and food security around the grain exchange and fertiliser trade.

strand_a.title: Accelerating fossil gas independence in Europe
strand_a.authors: Lukas Franken, Iegor Riepin, T H Brown
strand_a.summary: Recent price shocks have prompted calls to curb Europe's dependence on fossil gas imports, but the cost of this goal, and the consumer protection it affords, remain uncertain. Here we address this gap by imposing constraints on fossil gas supply in a European energy system model that co-optimises abatement across all gas uses at high spatio-temporal resolution. Cutting import reliance proves economically compelling: through savings in power generation and low-temperature heat in industry and buildings, Europe can halve its natural gas consumption for 16bnEUR/a, aligning demand with the continent's production capacity of 200 bcm.

strand_a.title: Cold War 2.0 and defence readiness
strand_a.summary: In the context of simultaneous rise of external threats through CRINK and the reprioritisation of transatlantic ally’s global posture, we study how a protracted low intensity conflict with CRINK would affect European allies’ preparedness to protect the security of the citizens and the integrity of the territory. As a worst case, we investigate the trade channel of geo-economic fragmentation in a Cold War 2.0 implying a complete cessation of trade with CRINK and a full blockade of Taiwan in an international multi-sectoral macroeconomic model featuring the defence sector and interlinking countries via global supply chains. Even this less kinetic conflict will create challenges for Europe’s security—challenges that will only grow more acute as the crisis worsens.

high_order_inference.publication_policy: Constant checking, sparse output, slow analytical turnover: qualified candidates compete for at most two higher-order slots per reader product, except Trends which may surface up to eight independently qualified opposing-movement pairs; incumbents persist unless they weaken or a materially stronger challenger displaces them. Every surfaced candidate has an explicit falsifier search.
high_order_inference.lifecycle_policy: Analytical candidates accumulate. One missed detector pass never retires a finding; repeated non-redetection only weakens it gradually, and no new finding automatically deletes an old one.
high_order_inference.candidate_search_policy: Only missing-link and falsifier searches are fed back. No candidate bypasses normal A/B/C admission.

lenses.passage: UCA leads Clusters4Defense, an initiative mobilizing Ukrainian and EU clusters as Defence Enablers in the Dual-Use/MilTech sectorб https://www.clusters.org.ua/en/clusters4defense-initiative/ . It integrates EU-UA cluster potential through prototyping centre networks, EDF access, supply-chain localisation, reskilling/upskilling, and cluster internationalisation — turning frontline innovation into scalable, export-ready production and strengthening Ukraine's integration into Europe's defence-industrial and innovation ecosystem.

strategic_classification.trend_action_passage: From 2022 onwards, the ENDR is funded by the European Defence Fund (EDF). ENDR has 3 objectives: Bringing regional organisations and clusters together to exchange best practices on how to develop defence-related development strategies, including the integration of defence industrial and research assets into smart specialisation strategies Facilitating the flow of information for funding opportunities (such as the European Defence Fund, and other EU structural and investment funds); and Promoting the development of regional clusters of excellence.
